---
description: Convert an image of a graph into a Graphviz Dot in an accurate way
model: haiku
---

# Goal
- Given an input image of a graph, convert it into a Graphviz DOT file that matches
  it exactly

# Workflow

## Create the Graphviz File
- Create a DOT file that matches the figure exactly
- Save the result in `graph.dot`
- Say in the DOT file how it was generated, with this comment at the top:
  ```
  // Generated by `.claude/skills/graphviz.convert_image/SKILL.md`
  ```

## Render to Image
- Generate an image from the graph description:
  ```bash
  > dot -Tpng graph.dot -o graph.png
  > open graph.png
  ```

## Compare and Refine
- If `graph.png` differs from the input image:
  - Find the differences in layout, e.g.,
    - Node positions
    - Node colors
  - Apply changes to `graph.dot` to approximate the input image, e.g.,
    - Use rank to keep the nodes in the same relative position
    - Change node colors to match the input image

# Verification
- [ ] Confirm `graph.dot` renders without errors
- [ ] Confirm `graph.png` matches the input image in node positions and colors
- [ ] The DOT file says that it was generated by
      `.claude/skills/graphviz.convert_image/SKILL.md`
